Part IV  Fundamentals of Oncology and Nutrition Support
Nutrition Requirements
Determining nutrient requirements is dependent on age, gender, weight, body composition, activ­
ity level, and clinical status. In the clinical setting, this can be determined via indirect calorimetry 
or equations; in the research setting via direct calorimetry. Direct calorimetry measures the release 
of heat, however, it is expensive and impractical in the hospital setting. Indirect calorimtery (IC) 
is considered the gold standard in the intensive care patient where most clinicians use a metabolic 
cart to estimate the resting metabolic rate (RMR), however it is not often used due to its expense 
and the need for clinical expertise. Equations for the healthy subject such as the Mifflin–St. Jeor 
are used to estimate energy expenditure. Those equations that are most often used in the critically 
ill patient include the Ireton–Jones or the Penn State equations as seen in Table 13-5. ASPEN
